spec:
One tool, three new arguments, one watcher line, one guard in the start path. No new action (tool counts stay 25 and 40), state file or event type; worker.py untouched. Function names are the anchors.

A. GPU apps and commands: `keep_running` (21-apps.mjs)
1. Schema:
 - `gpu` (boolean): "Only for a new app or job: it uses the Spark’s GPU. Say memoryGB too."
 - `command` (array, at most 40 strings of 1 to 300 characters, without the invisible characters `env` refuses): the words to run in the image.
 - `once` (boolean): part B.
 - `memoryGB` maximum 32 becomes 112. `port` stays required unless `once`.
 - The three names join the "give only spark and container" check for restart and stop.
2. `appLook` also returns `gpu` (label `spark.gpu`), `job` (label `spark.job`), `cmd` (`Config.Cmd`) and `gpuOthers`: one more line in its command, `docker ps --filter label=spark.gpu=1 --format 'gpuapp\t{{.Names}}'`, without this container. For a job, `volumes` leaves out B's two mounts.
3. `appDiffers` also says when `gpu`, `once` or `command` differ from what the container was made with.
4. `appRunCommand`: with `a.gpu`, add `--label spark.gpu=1 --gpus all --shm-size 2g`. `a.command` follows the image, each word through `q`. Never `--privileged`, `--network`, `--ipc` or `--entrypoint`.
5. In `run`, before both starts (a new container; one that is there but stopped), when it uses the GPU:
 - a new one without `memoryGB` is refused: "A GPU app or job needs its memory figure (memoryGB)."
 - new `gpuAlone(sp, look, at)` answers 409 when `sp.deployments` has a running model (not role main), `sp.external` isn't empty, or `look.gpuOthers` isn't empty: "<Spark> runs <names> now. A GPU app or job has a Spark’s GPU to itself. Stop that first, or pick another Spark."
 - then `appRoom` with the figure, as today.
 Self-healing's bring-back runs the same lines.
6. A `command` word that `maskSecrets` would change is refused, like a secret setting.
7. `appNamed` (at once only as typed): also every `command` word as a whole word; with `gpu`, the word "gpu" and the figure ("24" or "24gb"); `port` only when given.
8. `changeLabel` (17-changes.mjs:94): the button also says "with the GPU", "up to N GB", the whole command, and for `once` "Run … once" and where its files go.

B. Jobs: `once: true`
1. `appRunCommand` with `a.once`: `--label spark.job=1`; `--label spark.chat=<ctx.conv>` when there is one; `-v "$HOME/.local/share/spark-portal/workspaces/shared":/in:ro`; `-v` that path plus `/jobs/<container>` at `/out`; `-w /out`; `-p` only if a port was given. Both paths are fixed text plus the checked container name, outside `q` so `$HOME` expands (as in `dockerRunCommand`).
2. New `jobFolder(viewer, node, name)`, called in the job before the pull: makes `jobs` and `jobs/<name>` through `sharedFolder` only (list each; `mkdir` what the worker says is missing).
3. New container: when `docker run` succeeds, a job notes that it runs and where its files go, and the operation ends. No `ranHere`, so `desiredAfter` adds nothing. No `appUp`.
4. A job that is there:
 - running: the answer is `already`, and `keepIt` is skipped, so it never joins the list;
 - stopped ("run it again"): `docker start` after `gpuAlone` and `appRoom`, as job type `deploy` with no `ranHere` (type `restart` would list it, 20-desired.mjs:19);
 - `do: stop` works without a list entry when `look.app && look.job`.
5. The end, told once. In `watchSpark` (19-watcher.mjs:126), after `knowledge.workloads[key] = next`:
 `if (next.labels?.['spark.job'] === '1') { if (state === 'running') delete next.endTold; else if (['exited', 'dead'].includes(state) && !next.endTold) { next.endTold = true; changed = true; if (!first) jobEnded(node, next); } }`
 New `jobEnded(node, w)` in 21-apps.mjs builds one line from the name (checked against the container pattern), the exit code and the two times, never the log: "finished", "ended with an error (exit N)", "ran out of memory", "was stopped" (`consoleStopped`) or "stopped when its Spark lost power"; then where its files and log are, and that it isn't started again. It records a `notice` event. If `spark.chat` (`^sc_[0-9a-f]{16}$`) is one of the owner's chats, the line goes there with `notice: true`, and through `tell('result', …)` when that chat's `channel` is telegram.

5. A Jupyter box still has no good sign-in: no secret is passed in, and Sparkie's log view hides its token.
